dossier.purpose: Serena (PyPI package serena-agent 1.7.0, MIT, by Oraios AI) is a Python MCP server/toolkit that gives coding agents IDE-like, symbol-level code tools (pyproject.toml:6-8,69-70). With its default LSP backend it launches per-project language servers (74 Python modules directly under src/solidlsp/language_servers/) and exposes, from one MCP server: exact symbol bodies/definitions (find_symbol with include_body, get_symbols_overview, find_declaration), references and implementations (find_referencing_symbols, find_implementations), symbol-level edits (replace_symbol_body, insert_before_symbol, insert_after_symbol, rename_symbol, safe_delete_symbol) and explicit diagnostics (get_diagnostics_for_file; optional get_diagnostics_for_symbol) (src/serena/tools/symbol_tools.py:36-738). Dedicated contexts for Claude Code (claude-code) and Codex (codex), `serena setup` commands and `serena-hooks` helpers exist (docs/02-usage/030_clients.md). It runs as an external MCP server process (tools appear as mcp__serena__*), not as a native Claude Code plugin, and its automatic before/after-edit diagnostics are implemented but switched off by default (src/serena/tools/tools_base.py:471). A separate paid JetBrains plugin is an alternative backend that adds move, inline, type hierarchy and debugging (README.md:98-120,141-182). Nothing was executed for this dossier; all statements come from reading the source tree at the tag.

claims.claim: 'Serena provides essential semantic code retrieval, editing, refactoring and debugging tools that are akin to an IDE's capabilities, operating at the symbol level and exploiting relational structure.'

'It integrates with any client/LLM via the model context protocol (MCP).' Clients either launch Serena as a subprocess via a launch command, or connect by URL to a Serena MCP server started in HTTP mode.

Agent-first tool design with high-level abstractions (symbols) instead of line numbers or primitive search patterns; 'your agent operates faster, more efficiently and more reliably, especially in larger and more complex codebases'.
'Do not install Serena via an MCP or plugin marketplace! They contain outdated and suboptimal installation commands.'
Two alternative backends: language servers over LSP ('the free/open-source alternative which is used by default') and the Serena JetBrains Plugin ('paid plugin; free trial available').
Language-server backend provides 'support for over 40 programming languages' (the README lists roughly 70 names, e.g. Python, TypeScript, Java, Go, Rust, C/C++, C#, Ruby, PHP, Kotlin, Swift, Zig).

Retrieval via language servers: find symbol yes; symbol overview yes; find referencing symbols yes; find declaration yes* (generally not for external dependencies); find implementations yes** (only some languages); query external projects yes; diagnostics/inspections yes. Search in project dependencies and type hierarchy are JetBrains-only.
Refactoring via language servers: rename yes (symbols only). Move, inline and propagate-deletions are JetBrains-only.
Symbolic editing via language servers: replace symbol body, insert after symbol, insert before symbol, safe delete.
Interactive debugging (breakpoints, variables, expressions, REPL-style) is exclusive to the JetBrains plugin.

Inside an agentic harness such as Claude Code or Codex, the basic tools (search_for_pattern, replace_content, list_dir/find_file, read_file, execute_shell_command) 'are typically disabled by default' because the harness already provides them.

uv is 'the only required prerequisite' (language servers may need extra per-language dependencies); install with `uv tool install -p 3.13 serena-agent`, initialise with `serena init`, then configure the MCP client with a launch command.

Evaluation: agents ran ~20 routine tasks and gave one-sentence verdicts (Opus 4.6 in Claude Code on a large Python codebase; GPT 5.4 in Codex CLI on Java; GPT 5.4 in Copilot CLI on a multi-language monorepo); 'Different agents in different settings independently converge on the same verdict.'
A memory system for long-lived workflows can be disabled; configuration is multi-layered YAML (global, MCP launch command, per-project with local overrides, context, modes).

install.method: uv tool (documented primary method; the docs state no OS restriction, Windows paths are documented at docs/02-usage/050_configuration.md:48 and CI covers ubuntu, windows and macos at .github/workflows/pytest.yml:83; uv is the prerequisite)
Post-install initialisation (default LSP backend; add -b JetBrains for the JetBrains backend)

install.command: git clone https://github.com/oraios/serena && cd serena && uv run serena

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - CI runs the full test matrix on ubuntu-latest (.github/workflows/pytest.yml:83); uv-based install is documented (docs/02-usage/010_installation.md:21-25); a linux/amd64 Docker image is built (.github/workflows/docker.yml:53). The README itself has no platform table.
platforms.wsl2: yes, with caveats - documented only in the JetBrains-backend context: docs/02-usage/025_jetbrains_plugin.md:155-176 recommends running Serena inside WSL with the project on the WSL filesystem; code normalises WSL/UNC paths (src/serena/jetbrains/jetbrains_plugin_client.py:248-272) and treats WSL as headless for opening GUI windows (src/serena/util/exception.py:14,33-36; test/serena/util/test_exception.py:28-35). No WSL-specific CI job or install section found.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes (indirect evidence; the README does not state architectures) - CI includes macos-latest, 4 of the 13 pytest jobs (.github/workflows/pytest.yml:21-24,83) with steps that branch on `uname -m` for arm64 (pytest.yml:378-383); docs list macOS ARM64 for the auto-downloaded C# server (docs/02-usage/050_configuration.md:483,508). The GUI log window is not supported on macOS (docs/02-usage/060_dashboard.md:12-16); Swift/sourcekit tests run only on macOS (test/conftest.py:450-451).
platforms.gpu: no - not used. No GPU/accelerator dependency or code path (pyproject.toml:19-55 lists no torch/onnx/CUDA packages); the only 'CUDA' hit is a .cu file-extension mapping for clangd (src/solidlsp/ls_config.py:437-438).

integrations.cli: yes - console scripts `serena` and `serena-agent` (serena.cli:top_level) and `serena-hooks` (pyproject.toml:64-67). click commands include init, setup <client>, start-mcp-server, start-project-server, dashboard-viewer, project create/index/index-file/health-check/is_ignored_path, tools list/description, config edit, context/mode/prompts management and memories subcommands (src/serena/cli.py:172-1520; docs/02-usage/020_running.md:105-178). Tools can also be run without an LLM or MCP through the Python API (CONTRIBUTING.md:52-57; scripts/demo_run_tools.py:25-51).
integrations.mcp: yes - `serena start-mcp-server` (src/serena/cli.py:232-400) built on the MCP Python SDK's FastMCP (src/serena/mcp.py:385-392). Transports: stdio (default), streamable-http (/mcp) and legacy sse, default bind 127.0.0.1:8000 (cli.py:264-280; docs/02-usage/020_running.md:34-79). Each Serena tool is published with readOnlyHint/destructiveHint annotations (mcp.py:106-112). By counting class definitions in src/serena/tools/*.py there are 52 registered tool classes, 29 enabled by default and 23 optional (e.g. all 13 JetBrains tools); the active set depends on context, modes and project config (docs/02-usage/050_configuration.md:59-139). One active project per server instance (docs/02-usage/020_running.md:72-77). By default every started server also opens its dashboard (src/serena/resources/serena_config.template.yml:38-49).
integrations.sdk_or_api: No separately published SDK or stable HTTP API contract found. (1) The Python package is importable and tools can be called programmatically (scripts/demo_run_tools.py:25-51; CONTRIBUTING.md:52-57). (2) Optional Agno agent integration via the `agno` extra (pyproject.toml:100; docs/03-special-guides/custom_agent.md:1-45). (3) HTTP: MCP over streamable-http/SSE (above) and the 'Project Server' (`serena start-project-server`, Flask, default 127.0.0.1:24225, POST /query_project and GET /heartbeat; src/serena/project_server.py:34-85; src/serena/constants.py:41; docs/02-usage/040_workflow.md:190-210). The dashboard exposes local JSON endpoints for its own UI without authentication (src/serena/dashboard.py:267-480); they are not documented as a public API. (4) A guide exposes Serena to ChatGPT via the third-party MCPO proxy plus a Cloudflare tunnel (docs/03-special-guides/serena_on_chatgpt.md:14-60).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Yes, both documented. CLAUDE CODE: `serena setup claude-code` runs `claude mcp add --scope user serena -- serena start-mcp-server --context=claude-code --project-from-cwd` (src/serena/config/client_setup.py:51-69; docs/02-usage/030_clients.md:102-141); per-project variant `claude mcp add serena -- serena start-mcp-server --context claude-code --project "$(pwd)"` (030_clients.md:141). The claude-code context excludes create_text_file, read_file, execute_shell_command, find_file, list_dir and search_for_pattern, is single-project and disables structured output (src/serena/resources/config/contexts/claude-code.yml:36-56). Optional alpha-labelled hooks go in .claude/settings.json: PreToolUse `serena-hooks remind` (emits a deny for built-in Grep/Read after about 3 consecutive calls, at most once per 120 s), PreToolUse `auto-approve` (allows Serena tool calls in acceptEdits/auto permission modes), SessionStart `activate`, SessionEnd `cleanup` (030_clients.md:149-226; src/serena/hooks.py:115-144,546-583). The docs state recent Claude Code/Opus versions show 'drastically reduced adherence' to Serena's tools and recommend `claude --system-prompt="$(serena prompts print-cc-system-prompt-override)"`, which replaces Claude Code's system prompt (030_clients.md:111-129; src/serena/resources/config/prompt_templates/system_prompt.yml:60-214); they also advise raising MCP_TIMEOUT if startup is slow (030_clients.md:144-147). No Claude Code plugin manifest, .claude-plugin directory or .mcp.json is in the repo (none found), and no PostToolUse diagnostics hook exists (hooks.py:595-634). Post-edit diagnostics therefore require the agent to call get_diagnostics_for_file itself (symbol_tools.py:482-533). CODEX: `serena setup codex` runs `codex mcp add serena -- serena start-mcp-server --context=codex --project-from-cwd`, or edit ~/.codex/config.toml; optional hooks need `codex_hooks = true` plus ~/.codex/hooks.json, and SessionEnd cleanup needs Codex >= 0.145.0 (030_clients.md:302-387; client_setup.py:72-88). The codex context excludes create_text_file, read_file, execute_shell_command, replace_content, find_file and list_dir (contexts/codex.yml:12-18) and tool schemas are rewritten for OpenAI-style clients (mcp.py:170-275,404).

readme.telemetry_and_network: README.md is silent on telemetry. The docs say Serena 'reports anonymous usage data' on startup (version, OS, language backend, dashboard on/off) and give an opt-out, env SERENA_USAGE_REPORTING=false (docs/02-usage/050_configuration.md:1306-1312). Code confirms: SerenaAgent.__init__ ends by calling _send_usage_info() (src/serena/agent.py:722), which GETs https://oraios-software.de/serena_usage.php with params os, dashboard, version, backend, context (1 s timeout, errors swallowed) unless CI=true, GITHUB_ACTIONS=true or SERENA_USAGE_REPORTING=false (agent.py:724-737). `version` is serena_version(), which appends the git commit prefix and '-dirty' of Serena's own checkout when run from one (src/serena/__init__.py:8-23; src/serena/util/git.py:11-22). NOT covered by that opt-out and not described in the docs: with the dashboard enabled (default web_dashboard: True, src/serena/resources/serena_config.template.yml:38) two background threads start (src/serena/dashboard.py:226-228) - one fetches https://oraios-software.de/serena_news.json with ETag caching (dashboard.py:719-762), one queries https://pypi.org/pypi/serena-agent/json for a newer version (dashboard.py:234-249; src/serena/util/pypi.py:12-32) - and the dashboard page's JavaScript GETs https://oraios-software.de/serena-banners/manifest.php for sponsor banners (src/serena/resources/dashboard/dashboard.js:94-113). The dashboard binds 127.0.0.1 (port 24282, higher if busy) and opens automatically on launch by default (serena_config.template.yml:49,70; docs/02-usage/060_dashboard.md:30,57-63). No account, license key or API key is needed for core operation; the LLM client is external. Optional network use: token_count_estimator ANTHROPIC_CLAUDE_SONNET_4 calls Anthropic's token-count API with an API key (src/serena/analytics.py:46-69; default is CHAR_COUNT, template lines 176-183) and TIKTOKEN_GPT4O downloads tokenizer data on first use (analytics.py:26-40). Runtime downloads: language servers and their dependencies are fetched on demand (GitHub releases, npm, NuGet, PyPI via uvx, Open VSX), version-pinned, host-allow-listed and SHA-256-checked for most (docs/02-usage/070_security.md:118-169; src/solidlsp/ls_utils.py:432-475; src/solidlsp/dependency_provider.py:180-248,317-369); the default Python server (Pyright) is launched via uvx and needs uv plus network on first use (docs/01-about/020_programming-languages.md:139-145). Local network services Serena can open: MCP over HTTP/SSE (default 127.0.0.1:8000, only if chosen; cli.py:264-280), the dashboard, the Project Server (127.0.0.1:24225, only if started; constants.py:41) and the JetBrains plugin client (port base 24226; constants.py:42); all loopback by default (docs/02-usage/070_security.md:100-116).

languages: JavaScript/HTML/CSS (dashboard front-end in src/serena/resources/dashboard, incl. bundled jquery.min.js)
YAML + Jinja2 templates (contexts, modes, prompts, config templates under src/serena/resources/config)
Test fixture repositories in many languages under test/resources/repos

entry_points.what: Console scripts: `serena` and `serena-agent` -> serena.cli:top_level (click group, src/serena/cli.py:141-162,1515); `serena-hooks` -> serena.hooks:hook_commands (src/serena/hooks.py:595-634), kept as a separate entrypoint for speed (cli.py:147-149).

`serena start-mcp-server`: MCP server (stdio default; sse; streamable-http) with --project, --project-from-cwd, --context, --mode/--add-mode, --language-backend, --transport/--host/--port, --enable-web-dashboard/--open-web-dashboard.
SerenaMCPFactory: creates the FastMCP server named 'Serena', wraps each Serena Tool as an MCP tool (SerenaFastMCPTool) and supplies the initial instructions prompt.
`serena setup <claude-code|codex|codebuddy|grok>`: registers Serena as MCP server in the client CLI (handlers in src/serena/config/client_setup.py:51-146).
serena-hooks subcommands activate / cleanup / remind / auto-approve for Claude Code, Codex, Grok, VSCode and CodeBuddy clients.
`serena start-project-server`: Flask server for cross-project queries (src/serena/project_server.py:34-85).

`serena project health-check`: starts a real SerenaAgent on a project and exercises get_symbols_overview, find_symbol and find_referencing_symbols; exits 1 on failure (used in CI: .github/workflows/python-versions.yml:94).
Programmatic use: constructs SerenaAgent and calls tool objects directly, without MCP or an LLM.

code.architecture: Three Python packages under src/ (pyproject.toml:106-107). (1) src/serena - agent/MCP layer: agent.py (SerenaAgent: config, project activation, tool-set computation from context + modes + project config, dashboard, usage ping; serial task executor in task_executor.py), mcp.py (FastMCP wrapper turning each Tool into an MCP tool), cli.py (click CLI), tools/ (Tool classes: symbol_tools.py = LSP retrieval/edit/diagnostics, file_tools.py, memory_tools.py, cmd_tools.py = shell, config_tools.py, workflow_tools.py, jetbrains_tools.py = optional JetBrains-backend tools, query_project_tools.py; base class, registry and markers in tools_base.py), symbol.py (LanguageServerSymbol / LanguageServerSymbolRetriever, name-path matching, diagnostics grouping), code_editor.py (symbol-level edit operations and application of LSP rename WorkspaceEdits; JetBrains variant), ls_manager.py (several language servers per project, restart on death), project.py and config/ (serena_config.py; context_mode.py = contexts and modes; YAML in resources/config/{contexts,modes,internal_modes,prompt_templates}), dashboard.py (Flask dashboard, tray manager, viewer), hooks.py, memories/ (project memories), jetbrains/ (HTTP client for the paid IDE plugin). (2) src/solidlsp - synchronous LSP client library forked from microsoft/multilspy (src/README.md:1-4): ls.py (SolidLanguageServer: request_* APIs, document-symbol and full-symbol-tree with pickle cache, pull + published diagnostics, rename), ls_process.py and lsp_protocol_handler/ (JSON-RPC transport), language_servers/ (74 per-language adapter modules that locate/download/launch servers; Elixir and OmniSharp keep resources in subfolders), dependency_provider.py and ls_utils.py (download with host and SHA-256 checks; hashes in resources/downloaded_dependency_hashes.json). (3) src/interprompt - Jinja prompt templating library (src/README.md:1-4). Data flow: MCP client -> FastMCP tool -> Tool.apply_ex (default 240 s timeout; language-server restart-and-retry if the server died: tools_base.py:330-441; serena_config.template.yml:141-142) -> LanguageServerSymbolRetriever / CodeEditor -> SolidLanguageServer -> external language-server subprocess. Global find_symbol walks the project's document-symbol tree (slow on first call, cached) rather than workspace/symbol (solidlsp/ls.py:2059-2065; serena/symbol.py:735-765). Symbol edits are computed by Serena from LSP symbol ranges and written to disk (code_editor.py:89-124,142-209); rename applies the server's WorkspaceEdit (code_editor.py:381-415). Per-project state (memories, caches, logs) lives in <project>/.serena by default (serena_config.template.yml:197-203).
code.packaging_and_release: Build backend hatchling; wheel packages src/serena, src/interprompt, src/solidlsp; distribution name serena-agent (pyproject.toml:1-3,6,106-107). Release flow is manual (README-dev.md:8-29): scripts/bump_version.py commits 'Release vX.Y.Z' and tags, updating only pyproject.toml, src/serena/__init__.py and CHANGELOG.md (bump_version.py:51-60,111-152). A pushed `v*` tag triggers .github/workflows/create-release.yml, which creates a DRAFT GitHub release whose body only links CHANGELOG.md; no artifacts attached (create-release.yml:4-19). Publishing that release triggers .github/workflows/publish.yml: `uv build` + `uv publish` to PyPI with OIDC trusted publishing (`id-token: write`) (publish.yml:4-30). Neither workflow contains a checksum, signature or explicit attestation step. .github/workflows/docker.yml builds multi-arch (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) images to ghcr.io/oraios/serena on pushes to main and `v*` tags, with BuildKit provenance (mode=max) and SBOM but no signing step; tags are branch, PR, semver and `latest` for the default branch (docker.yml:3-6,42-60). The Dockerfile uses python:3.11-slim, has no USER (runs as root) and bootstraps nvm, uv and rustup via curl|sh (Dockerfile:2,30,42,48-51). Other distribution: `uvx --from git+...`, `nix run github:oraios/serena` (flake.nix via uv2nix), and an MCP-registry manifest server.json that is stale at 1.5.3 (server.json:6,15). uv.lock exists but uvx-from-git ignores it, hence exact pins in pyproject.toml (pyproject.toml:44-45; docs/02-usage/070_security.md:171-175). Runtime-downloaded language-server artifacts are checked against src/solidlsp/resources/downloaded_dependency_hashes.json (src/solidlsp/dependency_provider.py:250-369).
code.tests_and_ci: pytest 8.4.1 (+ pytest-xdist, pytest-timeout, syrupy snapshots), ruff 0.12.5 and ty 0.0.24 configured in pyproject.toml:76-92,164-184,319-385. About 188 test_*.py files under test/: 28 in test/serena (agent, tools, CLI, hooks, MCP, dashboard, symbol editing, memories) and roughly 160 in test/solidlsp (mostly per-language integration tests that start real language servers against fixture repos in test/resources/repos); central skip logic in test/conftest.py:405-504. CI = 8 workflow files in .github/workflows: pytest.yml (OS matrix ubuntu/windows/macos x 5 marker-based batches jvm/native/other-langs/niche[ubuntu only]/catch-all = 13 jobs, Python 3.11 only; runs `uv run poe test -m <markers>`; ruff lint/format and ty type-check once per OS; language-server caches; no xdist by design: pytest.yml:4-24,83-99,151-155,774-781), python-versions.yml (`uv sync --extra dev --locked` plus `serena project health-check` smoke test on Python 3.11-3.14, Linux only: lines 58-94), codeql.yml (actions, javascript-typescript, python; push/PR to main + weekly cron), codespell.yml, docs.yaml (sphinx/jupyter-book build, GitHub Pages deploy from main), docker.yml, create-release.yml, publish.yml. Known gaps visible in the repo: F# and BSL tests are always disabled, Kotlin tests are disabled on CI, Erlang is not run in CI, Swift runs only on macOS, Haskell/QML/Gleam only on Linux (test/conftest.py:424-426,450-451,492-493; pytest.yml:172-185,586-611). CI results themselves were not inspected.
code.dependencies: pyproject.toml: 33 direct runtime dependencies in [project].dependencies (32 cross-platform + pythonnet for win32), every one pinned with ==, including 7 transitive packages pinned for security alerts (urllib3, werkzeug, starlette, python-multipart, filelock, cryptography, regex: pyproject.toml:44-52). Optional extras: dev (21), agno (2), google (1) (pyproject.toml:72-101). Notable: mcp 1.28.1, flask 3.1.3, pydantic 2.12.5, anthropic 0.117.0 and tiktoken 0.12.0 (used only by optional token-count estimators, yet anthropic is imported at module import time: src/serena/analytics.py:11), pywebview 6.2 and pystray 0.19.5 (dashboard app window/tray), pygls 2.1.1 (custom mSL language server), sensai-utils 1.5.0. Lockfile: uv.lock at repo root (CI installs with --locked: pytest.yml:147); flake.nix/flake.lock (5 flake inputs) for Nix. Requires Python >=3.11,<3.15 (pyproject.toml:11). Per-language servers and toolchains (Node/npm, JDK, .NET, rustup, gopls, etc.) are additional runtime dependencies, downloaded or required per language (docs/01-about/020_programming-languages.md:28-188). Vendored/forked code: src/solidlsp (fork of microsoft/multilspy) and src/interprompt (src/README.md:1-4).
code.security_policy: none - no SECURITY.md in the repo root, .github/ or docs/ (glob found none). Closest: docs/02-usage/070_security.md:1-34 states the trust model (local machine, MCP client/LLM, repository, user config and package-manager config are trusted), says shell execution and file modification are intended functionality, welcomes advisories only for violations of that model and recommends sandboxing. Related controls: trusted_project_path_patterns (src/serena/resources/serena_config.template.yml:205-218; 070_security.md:47-98), per-project read_only flag that disables editing tools (project.template.yml:112-115), pinned + hashed language-server downloads (070_security.md:137-154), CodeQL workflow (.github/workflows/codeql.yml).

claim_checks.claim: 'It integrates with any client/LLM via the model context protocol (MCP).' (README.md:19)
claim_checks.evidence: MCP server implemented with FastMCP (src/serena/mcp.py:385-392) over stdio/sse/streamable-http (src/serena/cli.py:264-269); tools carry readOnlyHint/destructiveHint annotations (mcp.py:106-112). Client-specific workarounds exist (OpenAI-style schema rewriting mcp.py:170-275,404; Claude Code structured-output workaround contexts/claude-code.yml:54-56; Antigravity 'does not fully support the MCP specifications' docs/02-usage/030_clients.md:610-614), so 'any' client is not verifiable from code but MCP itself is real.

claim_checks.claim: Language-server backend is the default and provides find symbol / symbol overview / find referencing symbols / find declaration / find implementations (README.md:100-101,141-151)
claim_checks.evidence: Default backend LSP: serena_config.template.yml:8 and src/serena/cli.py:178-185. Tools exist and are default-enabled: GetSymbolsOverviewTool, FindSymbolTool (name-path patterns, include_body, depth, substring matching), FindReferencingSymbolsTool (returns referencing symbols with 1 line of context before/after, symbol_tools.py:296-307), FindImplementationsTool, FindDeclarationTool (regex with one group that must match uniquely, symbol_tools.py:399-479) at src/serena/tools/symbol_tools.py:36-479. Caveats: global find_symbol scans the document-symbol tree of all project files, slow on first call (src/solidlsp/ls.py:2059-2065; src/serena/symbol.py:735-765); find_implementations availability depends on the language server (ls_config.py:377-381).

claim_checks.claim: Symbolic editing (replace symbol body, insert before/after, safe delete) and rename 'yes (only symbols)' via language servers (README.md:160-176)
claim_checks.evidence: ReplaceSymbolBodyTool, InsertAfterSymbolTool, InsertBeforeSymbolTool (symbol_tools.py:585-667), RenameSymbolTool (670-695, applies the server's rename WorkspaceEdit: src/serena/code_editor.py:381-415), SafeDeleteSymbol (refuses and lists references if any exist, symbol_tools.py:698-738). Body/insert edits are computed by Serena from LSP symbol ranges and written to disk (code_editor.py:89-124,142-209), not delegated as LSP edits. Move/inline/type hierarchy exist only as jet_brains_* tools (tools/jetbrains_tools.py:145,235,409), matching the README table.

README.md:151 (Retrieval table) is met by the default-on get_diagnostics_for_file (src/serena/tools/symbol_tools.py:482-533; optional get_diagnostics_for_symbol at src/serena/tools/symbol_tools.py:536-582); the README makes no claim about automatic diagnostics. Separately, an undocumented per-edit diagnostics mechanism exists but is disabled (src/serena/tools/tools_base.py:471-477). Caveats: default-on applies to the default language-server backend, because the JetBrains backend's internal mode excludes both LSP diagnostics tools (src/serena/resources/config/internal_modes/jetbrains.yml:12-13; src/serena/agent.py:1117-1118). The before/after-edit mechanism (EditingToolWithDiagnostics.DiagnosticsContext) is switched off by ENABLE_DIAGNOSTICS = False with the stated reason that per-edit diagnostics are 'a questionable feature' (src/serena/tools/tools_base.py:466-519); only tests and a demo script flip it (test/serena/test_serena_agent.py:1258,1289; scripts/demo_diagnostics.py:78) and no config key or doc exposes it. Diagnostics come from LSP pull requests with a fallback wait of 2.5 s for published diagnostics and an empty result if none arrive (src/solidlsp/ls.py:915-919,963-1038).

claim_checks.claim: Inside Claude Code or Codex the basic tools 'are typically disabled by default' (README.md:186-194)

risks: Post-edit diagnostics are off by default and Serena is an external MCP server, not a native Claude Code LSP integration. EditingToolWithDiagnostics.ENABLE_DIAGNOSTICS = False, with the comment that per-edit diagnostics are 'a questionable feature' (src/serena/tools/tools_base.py:471-477); no config key or doc exposes a switch (flipped only in test/serena/test_serena_agent.py:1258,1289 and scripts/demo_diagnostics.py:78). Diagnostics are available only when the agent explicitly calls get_diagnostics_for_file (default-on) or get_diagnostics_for_symbol (optional) (symbol_tools.py:482-582); the LSP pull request falls back to waiting 2.5 s for published diagnostics and returns an empty list if none arrive (src/solidlsp/ls.py:915-919,963-1038). The Claude Code integration is `claude mcp add` plus optional hooks (docs/02-usage/030_clients.md:102-226); no PostToolUse diagnostics hook exists (src/serena/hooks.py:595-634).

Claude Code use depends on prompt and hook steering. Docs state recent Claude Code/Opus versions show 'drastically reduced adherence' to Serena's tools and recommend replacing Claude Code's system prompt with `claude --system-prompt=...` plus alpha-labelled hooks (docs/02-usage/030_clients.md:111-129,149-157). The remind hook can deny built-in Grep/Read after about 3 consecutive calls (src/serena/hooks.py:149-163,479-521). The auto-approve hook allows any Serena MCP tool call whose name contains 'serena' and none of a short list of substrings (so editing tools like replace_content qualify) when Claude Code is in acceptEdits/auto mode (hooks.py:52-66,109-112,546-583). The override prompt is static text that names tools (type_hierarchy, inline_symbol, _move) which exist only as jet_brains_* tools under the JetBrains backend, and hard-codes a 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context)' commit trailer (src/serena/resources/config/prompt_templates/system_prompt.yml:84-94,181-182; src/serena/resources/config/internal_modes/jetbrains.yml:14-27).

Network calls beyond the documented opt-out. Besides the documented startup usage ping (opt-out SERENA_USAGE_REPORTING=false; src/serena/agent.py:724-737; docs/02-usage/050_configuration.md:1306-1312), the default-on dashboard fetches https://oraios-software.de/serena_news.json and queries PyPI for newer versions in background threads (src/serena/dashboard.py:226-249,719-762), and the dashboard page loads a banner manifest from https://oraios-software.de/serena-banners/manifest.php and builds HTML from its fields by string concatenation (src/serena/resources/dashboard/dashboard.js:94-113). The env opt-out is read only at agent.py:725; the docs do not describe the news/PyPI/banner requests (docs/02-usage/010_installation.md:42-45 only says the dashboard announces releases); the only switch visible in code is disabling the dashboard (web_dashboard: False, serena_config.template.yml:38). The usage ping runs on every SerenaAgent construction (agent.py:722), including CLI commands that build an agent.

Local HTTP surfaces are unauthenticated. The dashboard API has state-changing endpoints (PUT /shutdown, POST /save_serena_config, /save_memory, /delete_memory, /add_language) and no authentication code (src/serena/dashboard.py:314-414); protection is loopback binding plus a Flask TRUSTED_HOSTS host allow-list (dashboard.py:211-212; serena_config.template.yml:69-78). The global config it can rewrite holds trusted_project_path_patterns and ls_specific_settings (serena_config.template.yml:97-101,205-218). MCP over HTTP/SSE and the Project Server are likewise unauthenticated; the docs tell users to add authentication via reverse proxy or firewall if they bind beyond localhost (docs/02-usage/070_security.md:100-116). The Docker image sets the dashboard listen address to 0.0.0.0 (Dockerfile:67).

Published effectiveness evidence is self-reported and covers only the paid JetBrains backend. Five agent self-evaluations written by the project (2026-04-13 to 2026-04-17) all used the JetBrains-powered backend; the methodology page says the LSP backend 'has not yet been evaluated' (docs/04-evaluation/030_results/000_evaluation-results.md:9-11; docs/04-evaluation/010_methodology.md:102-107), and the methodology assessment was itself written by Claude Opus 4.6 (010_methodology.md:65-70). Reports show larger payloads than built-ins for small edits (010_cc_on_tianshou.md:138-147) and a move that created a circular import (040_glm_on_tianshou.md:38-43). README attribution differs from the result docs (README.md:48 vs 010_cc_on_tianshou.md:8; README.md:52-54 quote absent from docs). No third-party measurements were found.

Language coverage is uneven and partly unverified in CI; many servers are fetched at runtime. F# and BSL tests are always disabled, Kotlin tests are disabled on CI and Erlang is not run in CI (test/conftest.py:424-426,492-493; .github/workflows/pytest.yml:172-185); docs label many languages experimental and the Kotlin server pre-alpha (docs/01-about/020_programming-languages.md:39-47,70-72,96-108,158-186). Tests run on Python 3.11 only; 3.12-3.14 get install + smoke test (pytest.yml:84; python-versions.yml:1-18). Runtime downloads (GitHub releases, npm, NuGet, Open VSX, PyPI via uvx) are version- and hash-pinned for most, but a missing hash entry only logs a warning outside CI (src/solidlsp/dependency_provider.py:356-365), npm installs are not lockfile-based (docs/02-usage/070_security.md:169), and the Haxe VSIX is verified only for pinned versions (src/solidlsp/language_servers/haxe_language_server.py:141-162). The config doc says .NET is auto-installed for C#, but the script-based installer is documented in code as unused (docs/02-usage/050_configuration.md:478; src/serena/util/dotnet.py:76-80; only definition found by grep).

Security model is trust-based and repository-supplied data is processed. All of local machine, MCP client/LLM, repository, user config and package-manager config are assumed trusted; shell execution and file modification are 'intended functionality' and advisories about them are rejected; there is no SECURITY.md (docs/02-usage/070_security.md:7-27). Pickle caches under the project's .serena/cache are unpickled before any version check (src/solidlsp/util/cache.py:9-18; src/solidlsp/ls.py:357-366,3019-3059). Project activation_command and ls_specific_settings are honoured only for trusted projects, but the code default for trusted_project_path_patterns is ['**'] and pre-1.6 configs keep trust-all, while the template ships an empty list (src/serena/config/serena_config.py:924-927; serena_config.template.yml:205-218; 070_security.md:95-98). Hook state is unpickled from, and cleanup rmtree's, ~/.serena/hook_data/<session_id> with the session id taken unsanitised from hook input (hooks.py:38-42,200-207,541-543). Recent releases contain security fixes (memory-name path traversal in v1.6.0; sandboxed prompt templating and trusted hosts in v1.7.0: CHANGELOG.md:31-35,373-376).

Packaging/doc drift, release provenance, maintenance and licensing. server.json (MCP registry manifest) is stuck at 1.5.3 (server.json:6,15); compose.yaml and DOCKER.md use a `serena-mcp-server` script that pyproject.toml does not define and a `production` build target absent from the Dockerfile (compose.yaml:11,18; DOCKER.md:116; Dockerfile:2; pyproject.toml:64-67); the documented Docker run example ends in bare `serena` without start-mcp-server (docs/02-usage/020_running.md:238; not executed here); Docker support is labelled experimental (DOCKER.md:1-3). GitHub releases are drafts without attached artifacts, checksums or signatures; PyPI upload uses trusted publishing with no explicit attestation step; Docker images carry SBOM/provenance but are unsigned, and `latest` is also built from main (.github/workflows/create-release.yml:15-19; publish.yml:12-30; docker.yml:3-6,47,55-56). Maintenance: run by the founders of Oraios AI, funded by sponsors and JetBrains-plugin sales with 'no business model' otherwise (docs/01-about/050_acknowledgements.md:3-11; docs/02-usage/025_jetbrains_plugin.md:35-36); CHANGELOG shows v1.0.0 to v1.7.0 between 2026-04-03 and 2026-08-09 (13 version headings, CHANGELOG.md:5-603) and this clone cannot show later releases. Downloaded language servers keep their own licenses (texlab GPL-3.0 as a separate process; Intelephense premium needs a license key: docs/01-about/020_programming-languages.md:104-107,133-136).
